title: The influence of BCG vaccine strain on mycobacteria-specific and non-specific immune responses in a prospective cohort of infants in Uganda.
ehr_evidence: Data were collected from the Entebbe Mother and Baby Study, a prospective birth cohort in Uganda, using questionnaires, blood samples, ELISA assays, and clinical follow-up.
summary: Prospective cohort study evaluating the influence of three BCG vaccine strains (Russia, Bulgaria, Denmark) on mycobacteria-specific and non-specific immune responses, scarring, adverse events, and mortality in 1341 infants in Uganda.
key_findings: BCG-Denmark immunised infants showed the highest cytokine responses, with significantly higher IFN-γ geometric mean ratios compared to BCG-Russia across all stimuli (e.g., GMR 2.24 for cCFP, 3.09 for PHA).
BCG scar frequency differed significantly by strain: 52.2% for Russia, 64.1% for Bulgaria, and 92.6% for Denmark (p < 0.001).
Infants with BCG scars had higher IFN-γ and IL-13 responses to mycobacterial antigens than those without scars.
BCG-related adverse events were highest in the Denmark group (1.8%) compared to Russia (0.3%) and Bulgaria (1.0%) (p = 0.025).
Mortality differences between strain groups were not significant (HR 1.22 for Denmark vs Russia, 95% CI 0.42-3.53, p = 0.87).
population: 1341 infants from the Entebbe Mother and Baby Study in Uganda, followed up to 12 months of age
limitations: Not randomised to BCG strain, potential for confounding by seasonal exposures
Underpowered to detect significant mortality differences
Could not analyse TB outcomes or long-term effects
Analysis was a post-hoc subset of the original trial
